ambiguities.impact: The recurrence should be applied directly for m>=1, with q_1 handled by the base case; asserting it at m=0 would require an extra definition of q_0 not supplied by the paper.
ambiguities.issue: The displayed recurrence does not state its own index range, although it contains q_m and q_0 is never defined.

ambiguities.impact: A formal reconstruction must either retain both local conditions or prove from the C_i definitions that the lemma's c_8 condition supplies the earlier c_1 condition.

contract_plain_english: For every finite m>=0, the paper gives a componentwise upper bound for the exact residual q_{m+1}. It consists of an m-step propagated initial term plus explicit residual-accumulation, u^2, and mixed-precision terms. The proof derives a one-step q recurrence from Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2, handles q_1 as the base case, and iterates the recurrence under the stated conditioning threshold. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3, Note, and proof]

source_evidence.observation: The setting is a real n-by-n linear system with positive unit roundoff u, nu <= .01, well-defined floating-point results, and componentwise absolute-value inequalities.
Only absolute, monotone norms are considered; the norm is scaled so ||e_i||=1 and extended to matrices in the usual way.

source_evidence.anchor: Definition of kappa(A^{-1}) near the top of the page

source_evidence.observation: Lowercase c_i denote scalar and uppercase C_i matrix quantities whose dependence on n is suppressed and which are bounded above by functions of n only.
The column-pivoted solve uses a nonnegative matrix C_1; c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-uC_1|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_1, under c_1u kappa(A^{-1}) <= 1/2.

The algorithm uses column-pivoted solves, x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1, and computes residuals with subtraction last. For s.p.r.a. the residual is accumulated in single precision; for d.p.r.a. it is accumulated in double precision and converted to single precision, with double-precision relative error bounded by u^2 and conversion error by u.
q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b and |q_{m+1}| <= uC_6|A||x_m-x|+(n ubar+c_3u^2)|A||x|+ubar u C_7|A||A^{-1}||A||x|, where ubar=u for s.p.r.a. and ubar=u^2 for d.p.r.a., assuming c_1u kappa(A^{-1}) <= 1/2.

source_evidence.anchor: Note following Lemma 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 second inequality
source_evidence.observation: The paper defines c_3,c_4,c_5,C_6,C_7 and proves |x_m-x| <= (1+u)|A^{-1}||q_m|+u|x| after shifting Lemma 4.2's index.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 4.3, following Note, and displayed recurrence in the proof
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 4.3 gives the explicit finite-m bound for |q_{m+1}| under c_8u kappa(A^{-1}) <= 1/2, defines C_8,c_8,C_9,C_10,C_11,C_12, and proves it from a displayed recurrence plus induction with base m=0 supplied by Lemma 4.1.

statement.algorithm_linkage: Lemma 4.3 is a finite-iteration componentwise bound for the exact residual sequence q. Its proof substitutes Lemma 4.2's second inequality, with the necessary index shift, into Lemma 4.1 to obtain a linear matrix recurrence, then uses Lemma 4.1 for the base case and induction for later iterates. It does not state a limit, convergence equality, or computed-residual recurrence. [PDF pp. 10-12/printed 825-827, Lemmas 4.1-4.3]
binders: n is the positive system dimension; A is a real nonsingular n-by-n matrix, b is an n-vector, and x=A^{-1}b. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 opening; PDF p. 8/printed 823, Section 3 basic-result context]
m ranges over 0,1,2,... in the final Lemma 4.3 bound. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]

u is the positive single-precision relative-roundoff bound, and ubar is selected by algorithm variant: ubar=u for s.p.r.a. and ubar=u^2 for d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, floating-point model; PDF p. 10/printed 825, Lemma 4.1]
C_i are matrix quantities and c_i are scalar quantities with suppressed n-dependence. [PDF p. 7/printed 822, Section 3 anonymous-quantity convention]
conclusions: For every m>=0, componentwise, |q_{m+1}| <= (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m uC_10|A||x| + n ubar|A||x| + u^2C_11|A||x| + ubar u C_12|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
The proof's one-step componentwise recurrence is |q_{m+1}| <= uC_8|A||A^{-1}||q_m| + n ubar|A||x| + u^2C_9|A||x| + ubar u C_7|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, recurrence in Lemma 4.3 proof]
The final result is established by taking m=0 from Lemma 4.1 and applying the recurrence inductively for successive indices. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, final sentences of Lemma 4.3 proof]
constants_and_indexing: The finite bound's iteration factor is exactly (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m, followed on the right by uC_10|A||x|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
The non-iteration terms are exactly n ubar|A||x|, u^2C_11|A||x|, and ubar u C_12|A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
The recurrence uses C_9 and C_7, whereas the closed induction bound uses the resolvent-defined C_11 and C_12 and the enlarged initial coefficient C_10. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Note and recurrence]

Lemma 4.3 starts at m=0 and bounds q_{m+1}; the recurrence's q_m term means its meaningful direct range starts at m=1 because q_0 is not defined. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q_{m+1} definition; PDF p. 12/printed 827, recurrence and induction text]
definitions_and_conventions: q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b is the exact residual of the unrounded corrected value. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, definition in Lemma 4.1]

All absolute values and displayed inequalities are componentwise; powers such as (uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^m are ordinary matrix powers. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention; PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
C_8=(1+u)C_6, c_8=||C_8||, and C_9=C_6+c_3I. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_10=C_6+(n ubar/u+c_3u)I+ubar C_7|A||A^{-1}|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Note following Lemma 4.3]
C_11=(I-uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_9 and C_12=(I-uC_8|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}(nC_8+C_7). [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Note following Lemma 4.3]
c_5=n+(c_3+c_4)u^2/ubar, C_6=C_2+(1+c_5 ubar/u)(I+uC_2|A||A^{-1}|), and C_7=(n+c_3u^2/ubar)C_2. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Note following Lemma 4.1]
For s.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)((1+u)^n-1)/u^2-n/u and c_4=0. For d.p.r.a., c_3=(1+u)(1+u^2)((1+u^2)^n-1)/u^2-n and c_4=1+u. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Note following Lemma 4.1]
c_1=||C_1|| and C_2=(I-uC_1|A||A^{-1}|)^{-1}C_1, where C_1 is the nonnegative matrix from the column-pivoted Gaussian-elimination error bound. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, equation (3.1) and Note]
error_notions: |q_{m+1}| is a componentwise exact-residual magnitude, not a norm and not the computed residual r_m. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition; PDF p. 9/printed 824, r_m definition]
The recurrence controls q_{m+1} from q_m, while Lemma 4.3 gives an explicit finite-m upper bound in terms of |A||x| and |A||A^{-1}||A||x|. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3 and proof]
exceptional_values: A must be nonsingular because A^{-1} occurs throughout. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, exact-solution and equation (3.1) context]

The inverses defining C_2,C_11,C_12 are used under the paper's smallness assumptions; no singular-resolvent case is included in the claim. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, C_2 definition; PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3 assumption and C_11,C_12 definitions]
Undefined floating-point operations and non-real exceptional values are excluded by the standing model. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
No nonzero-component assumption on x or q_m appears. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3 and recurrence]
higher_order_terms: No big-O term is present: all retained orders are explicit as u times the iteration factor, n ubar, u^2, and ubar u. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]

Under s.p.r.a. (ubar=u), the residual-accumulation term n ubar is first order and the cross term ubar u is second order; under d.p.r.a. (ubar=u^2), these become second and third order respectively. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, ubar definition; PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
hypotheses: The iterates arise from Section 4's column-pivoted iterative-refinement algorithm, with residual subtraction performed last and the stated s.p.r.a./d.p.r.a. choices. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm and precision definitions]
The final Lemma 4.3 bound assumes c_8 u kappa(A^{-1}) <= 1/2. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3]
kappa(A^{-1})=|| |A||A^{-1}| || for an inherited absolute matrix norm. [PDF p. 5/printed 820, kappa definition; PDF p. 4/printed 819, absolute-norm convention]
The recurrence displayed in the proof is stated under c_1 u kappa(A^{-1}) <= 1/2. [PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3 proof]
The standing floating-point assumptions include nu <= .01 and well-defined operations. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
implicit_context: The final bound combines Lemma 4.1's residual estimate with the second, forward-error inequality of Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 12/printed 827, Lemma 4.3 proof]

The anonymous C_i and c_i are asserted to be bounded above by functions of n only; their displayed formulas retain u, A, and inverse factors whose boundedness is controlled by the standing smallness assumptions. The initial index is q_1: x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1, so Lemma 4.1 supplies the m=0 base case. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, initialization; PDF p. 10/printed 825, Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 12/printed 827, induction proof]

ubar=u for s.p.r.a. and ubar=u^2 for d.p.r.a. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, Lemma 4.1]
